summary: H.R. 10642, the Stop the Settlements Act, requires the U.S. government to place mandatory and discretionary sanctions on foreign individuals and entities involved in building, expanding, or financing Israeli settlements, outposts, or related infrastructure in the West Bank or Gaza. The bill also bans the import of goods produced in those settlements into the United States, directs financial regulators to issue guidance on related activities, and terminates all provisions after 10 years.

affected_groups.effect: Face mandatory asset blocking and visa denials or revocations if they participate in settlement construction, infrastructure, or population transfers after September 30, 2026.
affected_groups.group: Foreign individuals and entities involved in West Bank or Gaza settlements

affected_groups.effect: Prohibited from importing goods produced wholly or in part in Israeli settlements or outposts in the West Bank or Gaza into the United States.
affected_groups.group: Importers and businesses dealing in settlement goods

affected_groups.effect: Required to receive and follow specific guidance from the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network regarding settlement-related financial activities.

key_provisions: Mandates asset blocking and U.S. visa or entry bans for foreign persons who engage in, or are complicit in, constructing settlements, outposts, or infrastructure in the West Bank or Gaza on or after September 30, 2026.
Allows discretionary sanctions against persons who participate in financing or maintaining settlements that undermine a future Palestinian state, or who support sanctioned individuals.
Requires the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network to issue guidance to financial institutions regarding settlement-related activities within 120 days.
Bans the importation of any goods produced wholly or in part in Israeli settlements or outposts in the West Bank or Gaza, starting 120 days after enactment, with exceptions for personal baggage.
Establishes a 10-year sunset date on which the entire Act terminates.

summary_detail.plain_summary: H.R. 10642, the Stop the Settlements Act, requires the U.S. government to place mandatory and discretionary sanctions on foreign individuals and entities involved in building, expanding, or financing Israeli settlements, outposts, or related infrastructure in the West Bank or Gaza. The bill also bans the import of goods produced in those settlements into the United States, directs financial regulators to issue guidance on related activities, and terminates all provisions after 10 years.
summary_detail.significance: The bill establishes significant new economic and travel penalties directed specifically at foreign actors contributing to Israeli settlements in the West Bank and Gaza, while placing a total ban on the import of settlement-produced goods into the United States.
